title: Invariance moments of a uniform sign
statement: Give the two-element set $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ the uniform probability measure, and encode false as $1$ and true as $-1$. This sign-valued random variable satisfies the invariance moment conditions: it is $9$-reasonable, has mean zero, second moment one, and third moment zero.
replaced: Let $B$ be a uniform bit and put $X=1$ when $B$ is false and $X=-1$ when $B$ is true. Then $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions, including finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$.
